rounds.text: Adani Power Ltd is trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic valuation, with a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 308 per share against the market price of Rs 207, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 32.8% [E46, E47]. The market's current pricing is overly conservative, as a reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies only 12.5% earnings growth, which sits well below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E48]. Furthermore, the company exhibits elite capital efficiency, generating a 10.21% ROA and a 19.76% ROE that easily outstrip sector benchmarks of 2.11% and 6.88%, respectively [E8, E9]. This superior profitability is backed by exceptional cash generation, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 20,514 Cr in March 2026 and delivering a cash conversion ratio of 1.58x where profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35]. Institutional confidence is underscored by a positive institutional money flow alongside growing domestic institutional ownership, which climbed from 0.76% in September 2023 to 4.07% by June 2026 [E44, E45]. Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% and borrowings increased to Rs 54,670 Cr in March 2026 [E4, E40].

Adani Power carries significant valuation and structural risks that are masked by its near-term return metrics. The company trades at a rich price-to-book multiple of 6.14x against a book value of ₹ 33.7 [E2], and its P/B premium far exceeds sector benchmarks [E7]. Shareholders receive a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reported profits [E4, E61], locking in returns entirely to capital appreciation while cash is heavily soaked up elsewhere. Free cash flow plunged to Rs -2,817 Cr in March 2026 [E36], driven by an aggressive capital expenditure build-up as evidenced by Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) surging 189.6% to Rs 35,053 Cr [E41]. This cash burn coincides with a substantial escalation in borrowings to Rs 54,670 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 39,495 Cr a year prior [E40], raising leverage and interest burden risks. Furthermore, fundamental quality flags point to potential interest cost capitalization [E62], and foreign institutional investors have trimmed their stake significantly from 17.51% in September 2023 to 11.76% in June 2026 [E43]. Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E10], [E13], [E19], [E47].

Conceded: [E2], [E4], [E36], [E40], [E41], [E43], [E61], [E62]. While the bear highlights a rich price-to-book multiple and a zero dividend yield [E2, E4, E61], these metrics miss the exceptional underlying efficiency of the business, which generates an ROE of 21.1% and a 5-year median ROE of 33% [E13, E27] that completely justifies a premium over asset book value. The surge in borrowings and negative free cash flow driven by a 189.6% jump in capital work in progress to Rs 35,053 Cr [E36, E40, E41] is not reckless cash burn but an aggressive, high-return growth spend underway to capture market demand, supported by an operating cash flow of Rs 20,514 Cr that fully backs reported profits at a 1.58x cash conversion rate [E34, E35]. Furthermore, foreign institutional trimming [E43] is forcefully countered by domestic institutions increasing their stake from 0.76% to 4.07% alongside promoter accumulation to 74.96% [E42, E44], resulting in positive institutional money flow [E45]. Finally, the intrinsic value gap points to a tangible margin of safety of 32.8% [E47], rendering the bear's structural worries overstated against the strength of operational returns [E9, E10].

Conceded: [E13], [E27], [E34], [E35], [E42], [E44], [E45], [E47]. While the bull points to strong returns on equity and a positive margin of safety, these metrics mask severe balance sheet and cash generation vulnerabilities that expose long-term investors to extraordinary downside risk [E2, E36, E40]. The massive negative free cash flow of Rs -2,817 Cr directly undermines the quality of reported earnings, regardless of operating cash flow figures [E36]. Furthermore, total borrowings have expanded significantly to Rs 54,670 Cr alongside a staggering 189.6% surge in capital work in progress, which compounds the risk profile and directly triggers warnings about potential capitalization of interest costs [E40, E41, E62]. Institutional sentiment is far from universally positive, given that foreign institutions have slashed their holdings from 17.51% to 11.76% [E43]. Finally, the equity valuation demands caution given a zero dividend yield [E4], an inconsistent operating margin trend [E32, E33], and a horrifying historical maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.2% coupled with a 54.0% annualized volatility [E54, E55].

Conceded: [E36], [E40], [E43], [E54], [E55]. While borrowings have expanded and free cash flow is negative [E36, E40], operating cash flow remains robust at Rs 20,514 Cr, fully backing reported profit with a 1.58x cash conversion rate [E34, E35]. The massive 189.6% surge in capital work in progress to Rs 35,053 Cr represents active growth and expansion spend underway, which directly underpins future capacity rather than signaling distress [E41]. Foreign holding contraction [E43] is entirely offset by strong promoter accumulation rising to 74.96% and domestic institutions increasing to 4.07%, driving positive institutional money flow [E42, E44, E45]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model explicitly establishes a 32.8% margin of safety with an intrinsic value of Rs 308 against the current market price [E46, E47], while the rules-based screen awards the stock a strong 89 out of 100 buy rating backed by robust 34% YoY sales and 47% YoY net profit growth [E63, E64, E66].

Conceded: [E34], [E35]. While operating cash flow is robust at Rs 20,514 Cr and backs reported profit [E34, E35], it fails to translate into free cash flow, which plunges to a negative Rs -2,817 Cr [E36]. The massive 189.6% surge in capital work in progress to Rs 35,053 Cr [E41] coincides with borrowings jumping sharply from Rs 39,495 Cr to Rs 54,670 Cr [E40], alongside a flagged risk that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E62]. The bull downplays foreign institutional abandonment, where foreign holdings dropped from 17.51% to 11.76% [E43]. Furthermore, relying on model-driven margins of safety ignores screen warnings that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E68]. Finally, the zero dividend yield [E4] and historical vulnerability featuring an 89.2% worst peak-to-trough drawdown [E54] and 54.0% annualized volatility [E55] undermine the security of holding this cyclical asset [E59].
